summary: Learn policy writing and regulatory drafting with drafting briefs, comment matrices, and compliance crosswalks. Build practical skills in 5 days.
lede: Policy writing and regulatory drafting provides a structured way to turn legal requirements, organizational priorities, and implementation constraints into clear policy instruments, rule text, and supporting guidance. You will learn to frame issues, shape policy architecture, write enforceable clauses, and connect requirements to practical implementation. Through hands-on drafting, review simulations, and document control, you will create drafting briefs, policy outlines, comment response matrices, compliance crosswalks, and an approval-ready policy package. The course also develops practical skills in managing definitions, scope, exceptions, cross-references, consultation feedback, version control, and review checkpoints.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who already handle policy, compliance, or regulatory work and now need stronger drafting discipline. It suits both individual contributors and review-level professionals who must produce clearer instruments, manage comment cycles, and support approval processes. Policy Officers who draft internal policy instruments and guidance notes. Regulatory Affairs Specialists who translate legal requirements into draft rules. Compliance Managers who review policy language for enforceability and control alignment. Legal Drafters who structure clauses, definitions, and exceptions. Governance, Risk and Compliance Analysts who maintain policy traceability. Public Policy Advisors who prepare briefs and drafting submissions. Regulatory Analysts who track comment cycles and drafting changes. Internal Audit Managers who assess policy control coverage. Corporate Secretariat Professionals who coordinate approvals and board submissions. Operations Leads who need implementable policies and escalation paths.
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop, a word-processing application such as Microsoft Word, and if possible an anonymized policy, regulatory draft, or briefing note from your workplace. Familiarity with formal review processes, consultation workflows, and basic compliance terminology will help you get more value from the exercises. The course is delivered at an intermediate level, so you should already understand how policies move through drafting and review in your organization.
